questions.q: What do many scientists predict about life expectancy by 2030?
a: People will on average live past 100
Most people will retire before turning 55
Medicine will stop adding extra years
Birth rates will fall below replacement
questions.why: The overview cites the idea of longevity escape velocity and an average lifespan beyond triple digits.

questions.q: Which changes does the summary credit for longer lives?
a: Better nutrition, medicine and health awareness
Cheaper housing and more leisure time
Smaller families and later marriages
Global travel and freer trade
questions.why: Lesson 1 points to medical breakthroughs and a more health-conscious, better-fed population.

questions.q: Which skills does the summary say will matter as AI takes over more tasks?
a: Computer skills, lateral thinking and social skills
Manual labour, physical stamina and obedience
Sales ability, negotiation and bookkeeping
Memory, speed and competitive drive
questions.why: Lesson 2 says people will need to work alongside machines and lean on creative and social abilities.

questions.q: At which points in life does the summary recommend taking time to explore?
a: In your twenties, mid-forties and seventies
In your teens, thirties and sixties
In your twenties, thirties and fifties
In your forties, fifties and eighties
questions.why: Lesson 3 names those three stages, which tend to be marked by big changes.

questions.q: How does the summary say our idea of retirement should change?
a: It should include independence, exploration and growth
It should start earlier and last much longer
It should rely mainly on state pensions
It should be planned by employers, not workers
questions.why: Lesson 3 redefines retirement around financial independence, trying new things and self-growth.
